Structured and Unstructured Knowledge

A row can be wrong. A document can be obsolete. A retrieved paragraph can be relevant without being authoritative. This lesson gives each kind of evidence a precise job.

A
Open the case file

The asset register and the procedure disagree

At Lift Station 7, the asset register lists Pump P-7B as “standby.” A signed operating procedure says it is the “primary wet-weather pump.” A maintenance note says the designation changed last month. Which statement should an agent use during an overflow response?

The register is structured data. The procedure and note are unstructured content. Those labels describe form, not truth. The real work is to identify the claim, its provenance, authority, time, and review state.

A database cell and a sentence are both evidence candidates. Neither earns authority from its format alone.

Preserve record identifiers, document version, page or section locator, extraction method, confidence, and reviewer decision.

Ask who may resolve the conflict and what workflow turns the resolution into governed knowledge.

Do not vote by format

Choose the defensible first action. Then read the case file as three claims with different authority and effective times. The graph should preserve the conflict until a qualified role resolves it.

B
Evidence promotion

A retrieved passage is not yet a graph fact

A vector embedding can help retrieve the procedure passage. Retrieval says, “Look here.” Extraction says, “This passage appears to claim X.” Review says whether X may enter the governed graph.

For this case, the candidate triple is Pump_P7B has_operating_role PrimaryWetWeatherPump. The statement needs the procedure identifier, revision, section locator, effective time, extraction method, and approving reviewer. Without those, it is a convenient sentence with a missing chain of custody.

Move the passage one state at a time

Select each state in order. Read what is added at that gate. The button will not skip from retrieved text to approved knowledge because that shortcut is the misconception this mechanism is designed to expose.

Document-to-claim evidence rail Provenance network
How to read it: Each state adds a different kind of evidence. Similarity supports retrieval. A locator supports traceability. A reviewer supports authority.

What the rail proves: Retrieval, extraction, validation, and approval are separate jobs. Combining them hides where error entered.
Evidence promotion desk Signature interaction

Begin with the authoritative source, not the extracted sentence.

Debrief: A knowledge graph does not eliminate document search. It gives retrieved content explicit identity, relationship, provenance, and review state when the use case needs those controls.
C
Evidence board

Choose the right representation for the job

Keep the full document for reading and legal context. Keep searchable metadata and embeddings for discovery. Extract named entities and relationships when traversal has value. Publish reviewed statements when a governed application must reuse the meaning.

Classify by evidence state

Inspect the three tickets, then classify the maintenance note. You are deciding what the utility currently knows about the statement, not whether the statement sounds plausible.

D
Investigation closeout

Design the structured-unstructured evidence plan

Choose one utility task where records and documents must meet. Name what stays in the system of record, what is indexed, what may be extracted, who reviews it, and when the graph statement expires or is superseded.

Close the case without erasing uncertainty

Complete the plan with a source locator and review authority. The final check tests whether another person can trace a graph statement back to the exact evidence and understand its status.

Questions from the evidence room

Is all unstructured content “dark data”?

No. It may be searchable and governed already. “Unstructured” describes its form, not whether the utility understands or controls it.

Are embeddings part of the knowledge graph?

They can support retrieval beside a graph. They encode similarity, while explicit graph edges name relationships. Treat them as complementary representations.

Should every document sentence become a triple?

No. Extract only statements that support a real question and can be governed. Keep full prose when nuance, obligation, or explanation matters.

Can artificial intelligence approve an extracted claim?

It can propose and validate format. Operational authority must follow the utility's approved roles and risk boundary.

What happens when a document changes?

Refresh the index, retain the new version, and supersede or re-review affected claims. Do not silently overwrite provenance.

Why retain a low-confidence candidate?

It can support review and error analysis, but it must remain visibly separate from approved knowledge.

Evidence boundary

The Lift Station 7 records are fictional. Retrieval and extraction can be probabilistic. A reviewed graph statement can still be wrong if the source or human decision is wrong.
